fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Detached Structure; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Walkway; Landscaped Area
fr.considerations: Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Single Access Point; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations:
• Clear or thin the dense vegetation areas to open sight lines along the access drive so responders can see the structures and move between them without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain a clear travel path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Install a reflective address marker at the entrance to the access drive so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly to distinguish it from neighboring access points, especially under low-light or smoky conditions.
• Keep the walkway between the main residence and the detached structure clear of vegetation overgrowth so responders can move on foot between buildings.
• Designate a flat, open staging area within the open lawn area and keep it free of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials so arriving units have a place to set up.
• Because there is only one access point, avoid blocking the driveway entrance or access drive with vehicles, trailers, or stored items at any time.
• Install a turnaround area or a pull-out space along the access drive to allow emergency vehicles to reposition without backing out to the road.
• Thin dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can reach and work around all sides of that building.
• Keep any gates on the property unlocked or provide a Knox-Box or coded lock so responders are not delayed accessing the site.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Mixed Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Vegetation Separation; Vegetation Along Driveway; Ground Vegetation; Single Access Route; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof and walls of the structure.
• Thin the tree clusters nearest to the structure to create open gaps between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants that grow directly against the foundation or walls of the structure.
• Thin scattered trees around the structure so their branches do not touch or overlap with each other.
• Cut back mixed vegetation growing close to the structure on all sides to create open ground between plants and the building.
• Clear ground vegetation within the immediate area surrounding the structure, leaving bare soil or very short grass.
• Trim branches and shrubs along the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches, leaves, and debris that could block access.
• Remove or cut back vegetation along the edges of the driveway that narrows the travel lane.
• Thin shrubs scattered around the property so they are separated from each other and from the structure.
• Keep the single access route free of any vegetation that could block emergency vehicle entry or exit at any point along its length.
• Remove dead branches, dry grass, and fallen leaves from around the base of trees near the structure.
